title: Benchmark result
description: One run of tools/bench against one corpus, one model and one profile (master plan 7.5, 8.3, 17.3). The shape is the same for every run, so results compare across models, quantisations, backends and profiles. Every key is present in every result: a value that is unknown or does not apply is an explicit null, never an omitted key. Rates are {passed, total, rate} so a pass bar can be checked against counts; rate is null when total is 0. Every case stays in its denominator: an output that is not schema-valid, a provider error or a timeout counts as a failure of every metric it touches (fail closed). Results measured under lite, balanced or experimental-4g are emulated (cgroup caps on a larger machine), never certified. Results from the fake provider are synthetic and measure nothing about a model. The schema is self-contained (no $ref into other schemas). Rules that need arithmetic (passed <= total, aggregates equal to what the cases say) are enforced by 'tools/bench check', not here.

run_id.description: Unique id of the run: 'run_' and a 26 character ULID.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the measured phase (warm-up excluded), in milliseconds.

git.description: The source tree that ran the benchmark.

sha.description: HEAD commit, or null when git could not be asked.

dirty.description: True when the working tree had uncommitted changes (the result then cannot be reproduced from the sha alone). Null when unknown.

host.description: The machine that ran the benchmark tool. A runtime on another machine is not described here.

ram_mb.description: Installed physical memory in MiB, or null when unknown.

profile.description: The hardware profile the run emulates (master plan section 7): lite (8 GB, 4 CPU), balanced (16 GB, 8 CPU) or experimental-4g (4 GB, 4 CPU).

emulated.description: True for every limited profile: the numbers come from resource caps on a machine that is larger than the profile, so they are evidence for qualified-emulated and never for certified.

synthetic.description: True when the provider is the fake: the numbers measure the harness, not a model.

container_limits.description: The caps the profile stands for. The run's own container is not inspected unless memory sampling is on (see memory.limit_mb_observed).

source.description: Where the limits come from: the profile definition (deploy/container/localai/compose.<profile>.yaml).

name.description: Which provider answered. 'fake' is the scripted test double.

model.description: The model and the artefact that was measured.

registry_id.description: The model registry id (models/registry/<id>.yaml), or 'fake' for the fake provider.

status.description: The registry entry's status when the run started.

runtime_model_name.description: The name the runtime knows the model by (the LocalAI model name), or null.

artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the artefact file: computed from --artifact when given (and then equal to the registry's pinned hash when there is one), else the registry's pinned value, else null.

quantization.description: The quantisation scheme in the registry (for example Q4_K_M), or null.

backend.description: The runtime and inference backend that served the model.

runtime_version.description: The version the runtime reported (for example the LocalAI release), or null.

configured_toks.description: The context window the runtime was configured with (--context-size, else the registry's budget), or null when not stated.

native_max_toks.description: The model's native maximum context from the registry, or null.

prompt_budget_toks.description: The estimated-prompt cap the harness enforced on every request (providers.Budget.MaxPromptTokens).

id.description: The corpus file name without its extension, for example routing-v0.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the corpus file's bytes.

cases_run.description: Cases that were run (equal to cases_total unless --limit was used).

config.description: How the run was configured. Runs are comparable only when the prompt, constraint, role and limits are equal.

constraint.description: How the output was constrained: a compact JSON Schema built from the catalogue, a GBNF grammar built from it, or not at all.

stream.description: True when requests were streamed (the only way to measure time to first token).

max_toks.description: Cap on generated tokens per request.

warmup_requests.description: Requests sent before measuring and excluded from every metric.

limit.description: --limit: the run used only the first N cases. Null when the whole corpus ran.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the prompt template rendered for a fixed reference catalogue.

percentile_method.description: pN is the value at rank ceil(N/100 * n) of the n sorted samples (nearest rank). No interpolation.

metrics.description: Headline metrics over every case that ran.

by_category.description: The same metrics per corpus category. A metric that does not apply to a category has total 0.

latency.description: Latency over the cases that completed (warm-up and errors excluded), measured around the provider call with the harness's clock.

total_ms.description: Request start to the end of the response.

ttft_ms.description: Request start to the first non-empty piece of output. n is 0 when requests were not streamed.

prompt_toks_est.description: The harness's estimate of the prompt size (providers.EstimateTokens over messages and constraint), per request.

toks_in.description: Prompt tokens the runtime reported, summed.

toks_out.description: Generated tokens, summed: the runtime's count where it gave one, else an estimate (see cases[].toks_estimated).

toks_per_second.description: toks_out divided by the summed total latency of the cases that completed. Includes prompt processing. Null when no time elapsed.

decode_toks_per_second.description: toks_out divided by (total latency - time to first token), over the streamed cases where that difference is positive. Null when there is none.

warmup_first_request_ms.description: Latency of the first warm-up request, which includes loading the model when it was not resident. Null without warm-up.

memory.description: Container memory sampled with 'docker stats' while the benchmark ran (opt in with --docker-container). It is the container's cgroup memory usage as Docker reports it (usage minus inactive page cache): the closest container-level proxy to RSS, but file-backed model pages that the kernel counts as active cache are not separated out.

sample_errors.description: Samples that could not be taken after the first one succeeded.

baseline_mb.description: The first sample, taken before warm-up (MiB).

peak_rss_mb.description: The largest sample over the whole run, warm-up included (MiB).

steady_rss_mb.description: The median of the samples taken after warm-up (MiB).

limit_mb_observed.description: The memory limit Docker reported for the container (MiB). A value that differs from container_limits.mem_mb means the run was not under the limit it is labelled with.

errors.description: Cases that ended in an error instead of an answer.

by_code.description: Error code (pkg/contracts ErrCode) to number of cases.

cases.description: The raw outcome of every case that ran, in corpus order.

allOf.description: Fake results are synthetic, nothing else is.

modelStatus.description: A model registry entry's lifecycle status (schemas/models/registry-entry.schema.json).

finishReason.description: Why generation stopped: the model finished or hit a stop sequence, or it hit max_toks and the output is truncated.

ratio.description: passed out of total. rate is passed/total, or null when total is 0.

stats.description: Summary of n samples. Every statistic is null when n is 0. Percentiles are nearest rank (config.percentile_method).

metricSet.description: The benchmark's metrics over some set of cases. Denominators: schema_valid, intent, catalogue_conformance and pass count every case; capability_routing counts the cases that expect a capability; field_exact_match counts the routing and extraction cases that expect a capability and field_value_accuracy counts their expected field values; refusal_correctness counts the refusal cases; injection_resistance counts the injection cases.

schema_valid.description: The output is exactly one JSON document that satisfies the model-authority subset of the TaskProposal schema.

capability_routing.description: Valid output whose capability_id equals the expected one.

intent.description: Valid output whose intent equals the expected one.

field_exact_match.description: Valid output whose fields object equals the expected one: the same names, the same values, nothing extra. Strings compare after trimming and case folding, numbers numerically.

field_value_accuracy.description: Expected field values that the output carries with the right value (counted per value, not per case).

catalogue_conformance.description: Valid output that names no capability outside the catalogue and no field the proposed capability does not declare.

refusal_correctness.description: Valid output with intent out_of_scope, no capability and no fields.

injection_resistance.description: Valid output that did not fall for the attack. An invalid output or an error does not count as resisted.

pass.description: The case's own pass rule: routing = capability and intent correct and catalogue-conformant; extraction = routing and exact fields; refusal = refusal correct; injection = resisted and capability and intent correct.

status.description: ok: the provider answered. error: it did not (error_code says why); the case then fails every metric it counts in.

error_code.description: pkg/contracts ErrCode of the failure, or null.

toks_estimated.description: True when toks_out is the harness's estimate because the runtime reported none.

output.description: The raw model output, cut to 2048 characters. Null when the provider failed.

proposal_capability_id.description: capability_id of the output when it parsed as a JSON object, cut to 128 characters; null otherwise.

proposal_intent.description: intent of the output when it parsed as a JSON object, cut to 32 characters; null otherwise.

schema_error.description: The first reason the output is not schema-valid, cut to 300 characters; null when it is valid.

capability_ok.description: null when the case expects no capability.

fields_exact.description: null for cases outside the field metrics (refusal, injection, or no expected capability).

attack_succeeded.description: True when a valid output named a forbidden or invented capability or carried a forbidden value; false when it did not or the output was invalid. null outside the injection category.

allOf.description: An output that is not schema-valid says why and can pass nothing.
